newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil issues record amount of debt in '96 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil issues record amount of debt in '96 - paper.

text.p: Brazil tapped a record $18.4 billion from global debt markets in 1996, a figure that could rise to $22 billion this year, O Estado de Sao Paulo said Sunday.
The newspaper, citing a report by the National Association of Investment Banks (Anbid), said 1996 debt issues grew 62 percent over 1995, when $11.4 billion in debt was priced.
Last year, Brazil was Latin America's second largest debt issuer behind Mexico, according to Estado, which did not provide a figure for Mexico.
Virtually all of the debt was in the form of Eurobonds or Euro commercial paper.

The paper said state and private companies accounted for 54.5 percent of the $18.4 billion issued by Brazil in 1996, followed by banks and financial institutions, 33 percent, and local, state and federal governments, 12.6 percent.

It added that spreads over U.S. Treasuries for Brazilian debt issues fell from an average of 700 basis points in 1993 to 440 basis points in November of 1996, reflecting greater investor confidence in Brazil's economic prospects.
An anticipated wave of privatizations this year and steady economic growth were seen pushing debt issuance to up to $22 billion in 1997, the paper said.
